claims.statement: Notion tools use the hosted https://mcp.notion.com/mcp server over streamable HTTP with a private thread owner's per-user bearer token; loading without an owner or token returns no tools, and initial catalog failures degrade to an empty list.

Each Notion MCP definition is wrapped with required on_behalf_of; on every call the wrapper validates the participant, confirms the login is the private credential owner, obtains a current token, rebuilds the named remote tool, and asks for reconnection if authorization is unavailable.

Notion's on_behalf_of participant resolution requires a nonempty value matching the triggering user's GitHub login and a verified active-thread participant; absent or unverifiable participant context is rejected.

The initial Notion catalog loader runs behind a stale-while-revalidate TTL cache with a configurable per-load timeout, and a timeout or exception yields an empty tool list rather than failing the run.

LangSmith LLM Gateway routing is optional and centralised in make_model: a workspace setting overrides the deployment default, and supported provider calls are routed with a LangSmith gateway key while unsupported providers or missing gateway credentials fall back to direct provider calls.

For executable non-desktop, non-summary runs whose credential scope is known, the graph factory concurrently loads generic MCP tools and private-owner Notion tools; if credential scope resolution fails it omits MCP tools, and generic MCP source order is instance, workspace, then personal when a credential login exists.

DynamicToolMiddleware initially exposes only integration tool names and requires the model to call load_integration_tools before use; it builds each requested group once under a lock, reports unavailable tools as non-blocking errors, and rejects direct calls before loading.

Generic MCP discovery is cached for 600 seconds using the source namespace, connection name, and revision; unavailable scope data fails closed to no MCP tools, while discovery failure for one connection degrades only that connection to an empty list.

Generic MCP connections have instance, workspace, and per-user Store scopes. Later scopes replace a same-named earlier connection completely, so a disabled or empty allowlist override suppresses fallback; legacy flat workspace_mcps records are migrated to the instance scope on first read.

Only enabled, explicitly allowlisted remote MCP tools are exposed under collision-resistant generated names. At invocation the wrapper re-resolves the connection and rejects a changed scope, disabled/deleted connection, changed endpoint, or revoked allowlist entry before using fresh connection credentials.

MCP connection URL and OAuth token URL validation permits HTTPS endpoints without embedded credentials, fragments, or secret-like query parameters; headers and OAuth client secrets are encrypted at rest, while public dashboard records expose only header names.

Saving MCP credentials can reuse authentication only from the existing record in the same scope. A URL change requires explicit replacement or clearing of headers, and an OAuth destination or client-ID change requires a newly supplied client secret.

MCP management endpoints are mounted under /dashboard/api: instance and workspace connections require an admin session, personal endpoints use the signed-in user's login, mutations have a same-origin dependency, and header-reveal responses are no-store.

Generic MCP OAuth supports client_credentials using client_secret_post or client_secret_basic and cannot coexist with an Authorization header. Tokens are cached by scope and encrypted secret, refreshed before expiry, and retried once after a 401.

The MCP HTTP transport disables environment trust and redirects, keeps every request on the configured HTTPS origin, validates that DNS results are public, and pins a validated address while preserving Host and TLS SNI.

MCP discovery initializes a session and follows paginated tool lists while rejecting repeated cursors and duplicate names; failures are redacted to safe diagnostics and loading failures produce an empty list for that connection.

The Notion OAuth flow discovers Notion metadata and dynamically registers a public client, restricts OAuth endpoints to HTTPS mcp.notion.com, and uses authorization-code OAuth with S256 PKCE; its pending verifier/client secret is encrypted in a per-login Store flow.

The Notion dashboard callback verifies a hashed state nonce stored in an HttpOnly SameSite=Lax cookie before exchange; desktop callbacks return a handoff to the desktop session so the browser does not exchange a code under an unproven identity.

Notion access tokens, refresh tokens, and client secrets are encrypted at rest. Credential lookup fails soft for optional tool loading, refresh is serialized per login, and an invalid_grant refresh failure deletes the dead connection and requires reauthorization.

LangSmith tracing uses LANGSMITH_TRACING and the LANGSMITH_PROJECT setting (with LANGCHAIN_PROJECT alias); LANGSMITH_API_KEY is used for sandboxes, trace links, and feedback, while LANGSMITH_ENDPOINT supports regional or self-hosted services.

Focused tests cover MCP source precedence and fail-closed behavior, connection/OAuth secret handling, public-origin pinning, generic wrapper and catalog behavior, and Notion wrapper refresh and degradation.
